intent: To highlight the significant disparity between the prevalence of overweight cats and the low awareness of this issue among their owners.

requirements.question: Must the video state 55% as the overweight prevalence among household cats?
Must the video state 9% as the owner-awareness value?
Is the 46-percentage-point gap required to satisfy the intent, or can 55% and 9% alone suffice?

units.claim: 55% of all household cats are overweight.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight
basis.note: The table entity label carries the 55% prevalence; the table value=1.000 is a normalized bar value, not the percentage.

accept: Overweight prevalence among household cats is 55%
55 percent of all household cats are overweight
units.evidence: A value label or bar/segment for overweight-cat prevalence must read 55%.

units.claim: Only 9% of the cats' owners know that.

basis.note: The table entity label carries the 9% owner-awareness value; the table value=1.000 is a normalized bar value, not the percentage.

units.evidence: A value label or bar/segment for owner awareness must read 9%.

units.claim: The disparity between overweight prevalence and owner awareness is 46 percentage points.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight
basis.note: First value used in the subtraction.
Second value used in the subtraction.

accept: There is a 46-point gap between overweight prevalence and owner awareness
Prevalence is 46 points higher than awareness
Only 9% aware versus 55% overweight — a 46-point disparity
units.evidence: Both 55% and 9% must be visible and comparable; the disparity should be shown as a gap/difference, not only as two isolated labels.

optional_valid: Framing the 55% value as a majority or more than half of household cats.
Expressing the disparity as a ratio of about 6.1x instead of only a 46-point gap.
Stating the U.S. context from the original narration, provided it is not presented as table-derived.
Showing both values in the same color because both table rows share color #C0392B.
